item.title: Green River from Bishop Branch FITNESS Hike, 10.5mi; 2,200ft — Wed Jul 22, 9:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group We head to the tropical part of WNC where we may see more foliage and flowers in bloom. The road is now repaired and the trails mostly cleared out. Our route includes waterfalls, cascades, and rushing water. There will be a few manageable water crossings. See map here: https://www.alltrails.com/explore/custom-routes/custom-route-74a221c
This route differs from our usual one in the Green River area, avoiding the fairly dangerous washouts along the Pulliam Creek Trail. We will not do the Narrows rope climb this time.
...If you sign up and change your mind even if on waitlist, change your RSVP to "not attending" to free up your reservation. Any rain cancellation will be posted by 7:30am.
PACE: All fitness hikes have a brisk steady pace (\~3 mi/hr), adjusting for trail conditions, and regrouping as needed. These hikes are specifically for conditioned hikers. Please be sure of your hiking ability before signing on.

item.title: Jack’s Old-Time Jam — Wed Jul 22, 5:00 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Grab some dinner and a pint while enjoying our long-running Old-Time Jam! Featuring many talented musicians from the local WNC area, our traditional Appalachian mountain music jam runs from 5-9pm every Wednesday night at Jack of the Wood! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Jam > Grass > Jam: The Saylor Brothers — Wed Jul 22, 6:30 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
The Saylor Brothers are a jamgrass fusion group from Asheville, fronted by brothers Will & Ben Saylor, of Brushfire Stankgrass. This project is a foray further into the realm of bluegrass jam, with more emphasis on improvisation piled on top of a structure of traditional bluegrass and innovative original songwriting. As a trio with Greg Stiglets on bass, the band packs a large sound coming from three acoustic instruments, and often adds a fourth player for further improvisational and bluegrass firepower.
Jam > Grass > Jam is not an open bluegrass jam but is a residency featuring a rotating casts of special guests from Asheville’s bluegrass/jamband scene.
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. item.title: Steve LaSpina Trio — Wed Jul 22, 7:00 PM — Hotel Eve Jazz
item.description: Steve LaSpina is a master bassist and composer who has been a vital presence on the New York and international jazz scene for over four decades. A longtime collaborator with legends including Stan Getz, Benny Carter, Phil Woods, Joe Williams, Mark Murphy, Clark Terry, Chet Baker, Randy Brecker, Pat Martino, and Jim Hall, LaSpina has appeared on more than 275 recordings as both sideman and leader. His decade-long partnership with Hall produced six acclaimed albums, including These Rooms featuring Tom Harrell. As a bandleader, he has released multiple recordings under his own name on SteepleChase and Ram Records with artists such as Fred Hersch, Ben Monder, and Jim McNeely. An internationally performing artist and dedicated educator, he has served on the faculty at William Paterson University since 1999. item.title: The Swannanoa Gathering Public Concerts — Wed Jul 22, 7:30 PM — Warren Wilson College Swannanoa
item.description:
The Swannanoa Gathering was established in 1992 as a vision of Warren Wilson College President Doug Orr and founding Director Jim Magill to host summer workshops celebrating the music and dance traditions of the southern Appalachian region and beyond.
Big news…Our staff concerts will now be open to the public!
We’re excited to be able to share our incredibly talented staff with Asheville and the surrounding Western North Carolina community. Tickets will be available for purchase online and at the door.
The Swannanoa Gathering is an educational program of the college, consisting of a series of week-long workshops in various folk arts held on the campus of Warren Wilson College just east of Asheville in the heart of North Carolina’s beautiful Blue Ridge Mountains. Tickets are $35 per concert. Event Details & Tickets https://swangathering.com/about-us/public-concerts/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Asheville Crokinole Club — Tue Jul 28, 6:00 PM — Taproom At Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

Summer is a season of wild growth. Fields stretch toward the sun, rivers find their own course, and life flourishes beyond the boundaries we try to impose on it. In the same way, there is a part of each of us that longs to move freely \~ to shake off expectations, step outside familiar patterns, and reconnect with our natural vitality.
This ecstatic dance is an invitation to listen to the untamed wisdom of the body. Through movement, we'll explore what happens when we loosen our grip on how we think we should be and instead follow the impulses, rhythms, and instincts that arise from within.
Together we'll create a space where the wild, authentic, and fully alive parts of ourselves can emerge and dance.

item.description: Visitors are invited to print their own keepsakes with Jessica on her vintage letterpress presses, each printed on sheets of handmade paper. Jessica White grew up in Taiwan and spent her childhood transported by storybooks and fairytales. Following a career in academics as the Professor of Printmaking and Chair of the Art Department at Warren Wilson College, she is now a studio artist in Asheville, NC, where she makes prints, books, and crankies. Her work has been exhibited internationally and can be seen in public collections including Yale University, Stanford University, Lingnan University Hong Kong, and the Art Institute of Chicago. She is the co-founder of Ladies of Letterpress, a member of the Southern Highlands Craft Guild, President of the Wood Engravers Network, and is the founder and lead organizer for the Asheville Zine Fest and Asheville Crankie Fest.
